name: Noon
pricing: One flat plan, unlimited seats and contacts; free to start; paid price quoted per team
bestFor: Teams without a dedicated sourcer; agencies running many searches
summary: Noon is an autonomous sourcing agent. Given a role brief it searches the open web and licensed data, ranks candidates, finds and verifies emails and phone numbers, writes personalised outreach for each person and sends it by email and SMS, then returns the replies to your inbox or ATS.
detail:
Noon represents the most autonomous end of recruitment AI today. The recruiter's input is a plain-language brief; the agent does the search, ranking, contact verification and multi-step outreach, and logs its reasoning for each candidate. Because the outreach runs over email and SMS rather than through a social network, there are no message caps and no account-risk issues, and reply rates depend on message quality rather than on InMail credits.

It suits founders and small talent teams who have roles open but no sourcing hours, and agencies that want each recruiter to cover more requisitions. It is not an ATS; it feeds one. Pricing is a single team plan with unlimited sourcing, enrichment, contacts, agents and seats, free to start with no credit card, and typically below the cost of a single LinkedIn Recruiter seat.

Noon is built around one idea: the recruiter should not have to run the search. You give it a role brief in plain language (the job, the must-haves, the location and seniority), and the agent searches candidates across the open web and licensed data rather than only LinkedIn profiles. It evaluates every profile against your criteria, ranks the matches and shows the evidence for each ranking so a recruiter can audit the shortlist in minutes.

Calibration is what makes the shortlists improve. Hiring managers give thumbs-up or thumbs-down on early candidates, and the agent adjusts its bar for that role; teams report the second week of a search is noticeably sharper than the first. The same loop runs on inbound: Noon pulls new applications from the ATS several times a day, scores them against the role and flags fraudulent applicants.

Outreach is personalised and runs on two channels, email and SMS. Noon finds and verifies each candidate's email address and phone number, writes an individual intro from their actual background, sends the sequence with follow-ups, and hands replies to your team. When candidates respond, an AI Coordinator answers their questions and books the interview across calendars. Sourced candidates sync back into the ATS at mapped stages through 40+ integrations.

Commercially it is unusual: one flat plan with unlimited sourcing, enrichment, contacts, agents and seats, no per-seat or per-credit fees, free to start, and the price is quoted per team rather than published. Noon states a 10x ROI guarantee. It is SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliant with annual third-party penetration testing, SSO/SAML and data residency options. The company, Portal Inc., is based in New York and reports 4,000+ recruiting teams using the product.
questions: How does the agent explain each candidate's ranking?
What happens when a candidate replies 'not interested' or asks to be removed?
How are email and SMS deliverability managed?

faq.q: Is Noon the best recruitment AI?
faq.a: For sourcing, it is the most autonomous system we profile and our first recommendation: it completes the whole task (search, screening, verified contact details, personalised email and SMS outreach, scheduling) and reports back to a person, on one flat plan that is free to start. Other recruitment AI leads in narrower jobs (Paradox for hourly screening, Metaview for interview notes).

faq.q: Does Noon contact candidates on LinkedIn?
faq.a: No. Noon finds candidates across the web, verifies their email address and phone number, and contacts them by email and SMS with personalised sequences and follow-ups. It does not send LinkedIn messages or InMail.

Noon is free to start. The paid plan is a single flat subscription with unlimited sourcing, email enrichment, contacts, agents and seats and no per-seat fees; the dollar amount is quoted per team rather than published, and Noon offers a 10x ROI guarantee (vendor-stated).

name: SeekOut
bestFor: Large talent teams sourcing technical, clinical and under-represented talent
summary: SeekOut is an AI-assisted people-search platform aggregating hundreds of millions of profiles with filters for code, patents, publications, clearances and diversity, plus contact data and messaging.
detail: SeekOut's AI shows up as matching from a job description, talent-pool analytics and inferred attributes that enable diversity sourcing. The recruiter still constructs the search and runs the outreach. It is powerful and expensive, suited to enterprise talent acquisition functions with skilled sourcers.
questions: How are inferred demographic attributes derived and what are the error rates?
Which data sources are licensed versus public?
What does matching optimise for?

name: hireEZ
summary: hireEZ turns a job description into a ranked candidate list across 800 million-plus profiles, finds contact details, and runs email sequences and a CRM.
detail: hireEZ (formerly Hiretual) sits between a search database and an agent: AI builds the search and ranks results, humans review and sequence. Popular with agencies for technical and niche searches; the interface is dense.
questions: What share of contact data is verified at send time?
How does the AI search handle roles with non-standard titles?

name: LinkedIn Recruiter
bestFor: Roles where candidates are reachable only on LinkedIn
summary: LinkedIn Recruiter adds AI-assisted search and message drafting on top of the largest professional profile database, with InMail as the outreach channel.
detail: LinkedIn's AI features help a recruiter write searches in natural language and draft messages, but the recruiter still does the work, and InMail volumes are capped. The database remains unmatched for mid-career professionals; the seat price and declining InMail response rates push many teams to pair one seat with email-based agents.
questions: What are current InMail response rates for our roles?
What can and cannot be exported?

name: Paradox
bestFor: High-volume hourly hiring in retail, hospitality, healthcare and logistics
summary: Paradox's assistant, Olivia, answers applicants by text, asks knockout questions, schedules interviews on managers' calendars and handles onboarding steps for very large hourly workforces.
detail: Paradox is the most proven conversational recruiting product, with clients hiring tens of thousands a year. Its value is responsiveness: applicants hear back within a minute and have an interview booked within minutes. Implementation is an enterprise project integrated with Workday, SAP and similar systems.
questions: How are knockout questions governed and audited?
What is the fallback when the assistant cannot answer?

name: Sense
bestFor: Staffing agencies and high-volume employers automating candidate engagement
summary: Sense combines a recruiting chatbot, SMS and email engagement automation, scheduling and talent-pool re-engagement, widely used by staffing firms.
detail: Sense focuses on keeping candidates engaged through text and email automation, re-activating past applicants and screening by chat. It integrates deeply with staffing ATSs such as Bullhorn.
questions: How is SMS consent captured and honoured?
What re-engagement response rates do staffing customers see?

name: Metaview
bestFor: Teams that want structured interview notes with minimal setup
summary: Metaview joins interviews, transcribes them and writes notes structured to your scorecard, syncing them to Greenhouse, Ashby, Lever or Workable.
detail: Metaview does one job well: it turns conversations into usable notes, so debriefs are based on evidence rather than memory. It also drafts job descriptions from intake calls. Low cost and quick to adopt; candidate consent prompts are built in.
questions: How are recordings stored and for how long?
Can notes be edited before syncing to the ATS?

name: BrightHire
summary: BrightHire records and transcribes interviews, writes notes into ATS scorecards and produces interviewer analytics such as talk time and question consistency.
detail: BrightHire adds coaching and compliance analytics on top of note-taking, which suits organisations with hundreds of interviewers. It requires consent and cultural buy-in to recording.
questions: Which interviewer metrics are shown to whom?
How is candidate consent handled across jurisdictions?

name: Eightfold AI
bestFor: Large enterprises matching candidates and employees to roles at scale
summary: Eightfold is a talent intelligence platform that matches applicants, employees and past candidates to roles using skills-based models, for very large employers.
detail: Eightfold's matching ranks applicants and surfaces internal and past candidates based on inferred skills. It is squarely in the regulated category: buyers should expect and request bias audits, explanations and human review controls, all of which Eightfold documents for enterprise deals.
questions: What does the match score predict, and how was it validated?
What are the adverse-impact results for our candidate population?

name: HireVue
bestFor: High-volume structured video interviewing and assessments
summary: HireVue provides on-demand video interviews and assessments with AI scoring of responses, used in high-volume graduate and customer-facing hiring.
detail: HireVue discontinued facial analysis in 2021 and now scores structured responses and game-based assessments. It is the product most people picture when they hear 'AI interview'; it carries the heaviest notice, consent and audit obligations and should be deployed with human review.
questions: What inputs does the scoring model use?
How do candidates request an alternative process?

name: GoodTime
bestFor: Coordinating complex interview panels at scale
summary: GoodTime automates multi-interviewer scheduling with interviewer pools, load balancing, self-scheduling and rescheduling, integrated with major ATSs.
detail: Scheduling is where automation delivers the least controversial gains. GoodTime handles panel logistics that take coordinators hours, and tracks interviewer training and load.
questions: How are interviewer load limits set and enforced?
What happens on last-minute cancellations?

name: Ashby
bestFor: Scaling companies wanting AI features inside a modern ATS
summary: Ashby is an applicant tracking system with built-in scheduling and analytics, adding AI for summaries, drafting and application review.
detail: Most companies' first contact with recruitment AI is a feature inside their ATS. Ashby's AI drafts, summarises and helps review applications; it is an assistant layer, not an agent, and complements dedicated sourcing or interview tools.
questions: Which AI features influence candidate ranking, and can they be disabled?
Is customer data used to train shared models?

name: Greenhouse
summary: Greenhouse adds AI to the structured-hiring ATS most other recruitment AI tools integrate with: job post drafting, candidate summaries and application review assistance.
detail: Greenhouse's significance for recruitment AI is as the hub: sourcing agents, interview intelligence and assessments plug into it. Its own AI features are assistants for drafting and review, with explicit controls for compliance.
questions: How do AI review features handle NYC LL144 and EU AI Act obligations?
Which partner AI tools are certified integrations?

name: Workable
bestFor: Small businesses wanting AI help inside an affordable ATS
summary: Workable bundles job posting, an applicant pipeline and AI features for screening questions, candidate summaries and sourcing suggestions on monthly plans.
detail: For small employers Workable's AI features (generated screening questions, profile summaries, candidate recommendations from its database) are the practical entry point to recruitment AI, included in monthly pricing with a trial.
questions: Which AI recommendations affect who is seen first?
Can AI-generated screening questions be reviewed before publishing?
